brief.subject: Diesel dips 6 cents; 33,000 drivers sidelined on English rule
brief.headline: Diesel eases to $6.292 as English-proficiency enforcement sidelines 33,000 drivers
brief.dek: Diesel fell 6.0 cents last week, roadside blitzes widen, Class 8 orders drop 36%, and the LA/Long Beach strike threat is pushed back again.
brief.lede: Diesel slipped 6.0 cents to $6.292 a gallon but remains up 9.3 cents over four weeks. Meanwhile, DOT says 33,000 drivers have been put out of service over English-language deficiencies.

sections.heading: Diesel Takes a Small Breather
bullets: $6.292 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-02.
Down 6.0 cents (0.9%) week over week, a modest break on fuel spend.
Up 9.3 cents over four weeks, so check that fuel surcharges still cover your real costs.

sections.heading: Roadside Enforcement Keeps Tightening
bullets: 33,000 drivers have been placed out of service over English-language deficiencies, according to DOT.
283 violations turned up in recent CDL blitzes across Virginia and Arkansas.
Small fleets should confirm every driver can handle roadside communication before dispatching through blitz states.

sections.heading: Class 8 Orders Fall Sharply
bullets: 36% year-over-year drop in North American Class 8 orders in October, per FTR.
Regulatory uncertainty at EPA, equipment costs and tighter budgets are holding fleets back.
Fewer new trucks entering service could help tighten capacity over time for carriers keeping current equipment.

sections.heading: LA/Long Beach Strike Threat Delayed
bullets: A possible strike at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach has been delayed again.
Employers and a longshore union local are still in contract talks.
Drayage and Southern California carriers should watch for disruptions if negotiations break down.

sections.heading: Congress Shake-Up Hits Trucking Policy
bullets: Election results will reshape the House Transportation & Infrastructure committee's membership.
Several current committee members will not return, affecting the highway bill and trucking regulations ahead.

brief.seo_description: Diesel at $6.292, down 6.0 cents; 33,000 drivers out of service on English rule; Class 8 orders down 36%; LA/Long Beach strike delayed again.
